questions.prompt: Points a player scored in 11 games: 12, 15, 14, 18, 16, 13, 17, 15, 41, 14, 16. Quartiles: Q1 is the median of the lower half and Q3 the median of the upper half of the ordered data; when the number of values is odd, the median is left out of both halves. An outlier is a value below Q1 - 1.5·IQR or above Q3 + 1.5·IQR. Give the lower fence, the upper fence, and the number of outliers.
questions.prompt_markup: Points a player scored in 11 games: 12, 15, 14, 18, 16, 13, 17, 15, 41, 14, 16. An outlier is a value below Q1 - 1.5·IQR or above Q3 + 1.5·IQR. Give the lower fence, the upper fence, and the number of outliers.
questions.grading_note: Form required: all three. Ordered 12, 13, 14, 14, 15, 15, 16, 16, 17, 18, 41; Q1 = 14, Q3 = 17, IQR 3; fences 14 - 4.5 = 9.5 and 17 + 4.5 = 21.5; only 41 is an outlier.

sections.skill: Decide whether an outlier is an error or a real value

branch.new_demand: Judge from context whether a flagged value is a likely error or a legitimate unusual value.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Decide whether an outlier is an error or a real value
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Heights of 9 adults in a study are listed in centimeters; one value is 17.5. Which is the most reasonable judgment?
questions.prompt_markup: Heights of 9 adults in a study are listed in centimeters; one value is 17.5. Which is the most reasonable judgment?

choices.text: Outliers are always errors, so every outlier in the data should be removed.
It is a real height, so it must be kept exactly as it is in the data.
It is probably a recording error (likely 175 cm), so check the record before using it.
It is an outlier, so it should be deleted without any further checking.

questions.correct_answer: It is probably a recording error (likely 175 cm), so check the record before using it.
questions.grading_note: An adult height of 17.5 cm is impossible; an outlier is checked, not removed automatically.
